comparisons.peer_topic: Company Business Description and Reportable Segments
comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom is a global technology leader designing semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions across two reportable segments: semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software, serving markets including AI networking, data centers, and enterprise IT.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose their reportable segment structures in Item 8, but they differ in the number of segments and their focus. AMD identifies four reportable segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) with specific product lists like AI accelerators and discrete GPUs. In contrast, Broadcom reports only two high-level segments (Semiconductor Solutions and Infrastructure Software) and describes its business broadly as a designer of semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions rather than listing specific product lines within the segment definition text.

sentences.text: The Company's four reportable segments are:

• the Data Center segment, which primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers;
• the Client segment, which primarily includes CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks;
• the Gaming segment, which primarily includes discrete GPUs, and semi-custom SoC products and development services; and
• the Embedded segment, which primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, System on Modules (SOMs), and Adaptive SoC products.
We have two reportable segments: semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software.

comparisons.peer_summary: Business is organized into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All other; CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry are reportable operating segments, while NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable segments with selective disclosure.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and Intel both disclose their reportable operating segments in Item 8, but they differ significantly in structure and composition. AMD has four equal-weight reportable segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) defined by product types (e.g., AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs). Intel has three reportable operating segments (CCG, DCAI, Intel Foundry) and explicitly lists non-reportable segments (NEX, Altera, Mobileye) that receive selective disclosure. Unlike AMD’s product-based grouping, Intel’s structure separates its foundry manufacturing business as a distinct reportable segment alongside its product groups.

comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose four reportable segments/business units in Item 8. AMD’s four segments are defined by product application (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) and include specific technologies like AI accelerators and FPGAs. Micron’s four units (Compute and Networking, Mobile, Embedded, Storage) are also defined by market application but focus exclusively on memory and storage products. While both have an 'Embedded' segment, AMD’s includes broader computing silicon (CPUs, GPUs), whereas Micron’s is limited to memory and storage for the intelligent edge.
